subject: English
source: Based on the uploaded Class 6 Poorvi Unit 1 PDF (fepr101.pdf), Reprint 2026–27. Story wording is not reproduced; this is an original study guide.
goals: Summarise the plot without retelling every event.
Explain how a character’s choices change the outcome.
Infer a theme from events and consequences.
Use context to understand key vocabulary.
Write a paragraph supported by evidence from the story.
summary: In this folk-tale-style story, Rama Natha is absorbed by the hope of finding a magical way to turn objects into gold. A sage gives him a task that requires sustained, practical work: growing banana plants and collecting dew. Over time, the work changes his habits and produces a real benefit. The story contrasts the wish for instant wealth with patience, effort and useful work.

concepts.title: Plot and turning point
concepts.explanation: The plot moves from Rama Natha’s unrealistic belief, through the sage’s demanding instruction, to the consequences of sustained effort. The turning point is not a sudden spell; it is the point at which the character begins a process that requires regular work.
concepts.example: When explaining the turning point, describe what changes in Rama Natha’s behaviour and why that change matters, rather than listing every event.

concepts.title: Characterisation through actions
concepts.explanation: A character can be understood through choices, habits and responses. Rama Natha’s early choices show that he is distracted by an easy promise. His later work shows a change in patience and responsibility.
concepts.example: A strong answer connects a trait to an action: ‘His repeated search for a potion suggests that he is attracted to shortcuts.’

concepts.title: Theme and moral
concepts.explanation: A theme is a central idea explored by a story. A moral is a lesson the reader may take from it. Here, the events suggest that steady effort can create value while chasing shortcuts can waste time and resources.
concepts.example: Avoid writing only ‘Hard work is good.’ Explain how the task of caring for plants turns effort into a practical result.

concepts.title: Fables and folk tales
concepts.explanation: A fable or folk tale often uses a memorable situation and a clear consequence to communicate a lesson. The events may be imaginative, but readers can still examine the characters’ decisions and the message.
concepts.example: Ask: What belief does the story challenge? What behaviour does it encourage? Which events support that interpretation?

concepts.title: Vocabulary in context
concepts.explanation: Use the surrounding sentence and the role of a word in the story to infer meaning, then check a dictionary if needed. A context clue may show whether a word names a person, place, action or feeling.
concepts.example: If a character is described as worried about money being spent, the surrounding events help explain why the character feels anxious.

workedExamples.question: How can you explain the central message of the story in a short paragraph?
steps: State the message: sustained effort is more useful than waiting for an effortless miracle.
Refer to Rama Natha’s initial search for a potion.
Explain how the sage’s task requires repeated care and patience.
Connect the outcome to the message without claiming that the dew itself is magical.
workedExamples.answer: The story suggests that useful results come from patient, sustained effort rather than a search for shortcuts. Rama Natha begins by hoping for a magical solution, but the task makes him work regularly. His work changes his habits and creates practical value.

workedExamples.question: How do you support a character-trait answer with evidence?
steps: Name one trait, such as impatience or persistence.
Identify a relevant action in the story.
Explain how that action reveals the trait.
Avoid claiming more than the event supports.
workedExamples.answer: Rama Natha’s repeated search for a potion suggests that he is strongly attracted to the idea of an easy reward; the repeated search is the evidence for this interpretation.

practice.question: Why is the sage’s task more important than the promise of a potion?
practice.answer: It makes Rama Natha practise regular care and sustained effort, which lead to a real-world outcome.
practice.why: The task changes the character’s behaviour rather than rewarding a shortcut.

practice.question: Write a two-sentence summary of the story.
practice.answer: Rama Natha searches for a magical way to become rich, and a sage gives him a task that requires regular work. The task gradually changes his habits and shows that patient effort can create real value.
practice.why: A summary includes the main conflict, turning point and outcome without minor details.

practice.question: What is the difference between a theme and a plot?
practice.answer: The plot is the sequence of events; the theme is the central idea explored through those events.
practice.why: A question about theme needs interpretation, not just a list of actions.

practice.question: Give one piece of evidence that Rama Natha changes over the story.
practice.answer: He moves from searching for a magical shortcut to regularly carrying out the work the sage has prescribed.
practice.why: A change in behaviour is evidence of character development.

mcqs.q: At the beginning, Rama Natha is mainly occupied with…
options: Searching for a magical shortcut to wealth
mcqs.why: His attention is fixed on the imagined potion.

mcqs.q: Which quality is most directly required by the sage’s task?
mcqs.why: Growing plants and collecting dew require repeated, sustained work.

options: A central idea explored by a text
mcqs.why: Themes express ideas that the events develop.

mcqs.q: Which answer is strongest when describing a character?
options: He is bad, because I say so
He is impatient; his repeated search for an instant solution supports this view
He is impatient and every person in the story agrees
mcqs.why: A well-supported interpretation connects a trait to evidence.

options: Focus on the main conflict, turning point and outcome
mcqs.why: A summary preserves the main arc in fewer words.

revision: Plot = events; characterisation = how a character is revealed; theme = central idea.
Use actions as evidence when describing characters.
The story contrasts shortcuts with sustained effort.
A summary is brief and includes the main conflict, turning point and outcome.
For literature answers, explain the evidence instead of merely naming a moral.

chapterTest.instructions: Write full-sentence answers. Check that each interpretation is supported by the story’s events.

questions.q: Describe Rama Natha’s initial goal and explain why it causes difficulty.
questions.answer: He wants a magical potion to turn objects into gold. This distracts him from managing his land and encourages him to spend time and resources chasing a shortcut.

questions.q: Explain how the sage’s task affects the story’s outcome.
questions.answer: It requires regular, practical work. That work changes Rama Natha’s habits and leads to a useful result, revealing the story’s message.

questions.q: State one theme and support it with an event.
questions.answer: One theme is that patient effort creates real value. The repeated care needed for the plants shows that the result depends on sustained work.

questions.q: Write a 50–70 word summary of the story.
questions.answer: A suitable answer should mention Rama Natha’s belief in a magical potion, the sage’s task involving banana plants and dew, the regular effort required, and the practical change that follows. It should not reproduce the story or add events.
